Class ALeastSquaresFitter

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.fit.ALeastSquaresFitter
All Implemented Interfaces:
IFitStringGetter, IFitter
Direct Known Subclasses:
ErfcFitter, ErfFitter, ExponentialDecayFitter, GaussianFitter, LorentzianFitter, MultiGaussianFitter, PolynomialFitter, PowerLawFitter
public abstract class ALeastSquaresFitter extends Object implements IFitter, IFitStringGetter
Base class for least-squares fitters built on Apache Commons Math 3.x fitting.leastsquares.

This class centralizes the common fit pipeline:

  • x/y/weights validation
  • weights-from-sigma helper
  • least-squares problem builder wiring
  • optimizer execution
  • best-effort covariance extraction
  • uniform FitResult creation

Concrete fitters typically only implement:

  • getParameterCount()
  • model(double[])
  • optionally defaultInitialGuess(double[], double[], double[])
  • optionally defaultValidator()
  • optionally getModelName()

Chi-square note (Commons Math 3.6.1)

Optimum.getCost() returns sqrt(sum r_i^2). Therefore: 
chiSquare = cost ^ 2
If you supply weights as 1/sigmaY^2 in a diagonal weight matrix, this corresponds to the conventional weighted chi-square.

    • validateWeights

      protected static void validateWeights(double[] weights, int n)
      Validate weights array.

      Commons Math accepts any real diagonal matrix as weights, but for typical least-squares usage, weights should be finite and non-negative (often 1/sigma^2).

      Parameters:
      weights - optional weights array
      n - expected length

    • weightsFromSigmaY

      public static double[] weightsFromSigmaY(double[] sigmaY)
      Convenience: build weights from y-uncertainties.

      weights[i] = 1/(sigmaY[i]^2).

      Parameters:
      sigmaY - y uncertainties, all > 0
      Returns:
      weights array

    • clampingValidator

      protected static org.apache.commons.math3.fitting.leastsquares.ParameterValidator clampingValidator(double[] lower, double[] upper)
      Create a ParameterValidator that clamps parameters to [lower[i], upper[i]]. Use +/-infinity for "no bound".

      This is a simple, robust bounds strategy compatible with Commons Math least-squares. It is not a hard-constraint optimizer; it repairs invalid steps by clamping.

      Parameters:
      lower - lower bounds (length p)
      upper - upper bounds (length p)
      Returns:
      clamping validator

    • fit

      public final FitResult fit(double[] x, double[] y, double[] weights, double[] initialGuessOverride, org.apache.commons.math3.fitting.leastsquares.ParameterValidator validatorOverride)
      Full fit entry point. This is the common least-squares pipeline for all derived fitters.
      Parameters:
      x - x data
      y - y data
      weights - optional weights (length n), typically 1/sigmaY^2; may be null
      initialGuessOverride - optional explicit initial guess (length p); may be null
      validatorOverride - optional explicit parameter validator; may be null

      FitResult
